# 2026 MCM Problem C: Data With The Stars

Problem C: Data With The Stars



Dancing with the Stars (DWTS) is the American version of an international television franchise
based on the British show “Strictly Come Dancing” (“Come Dancing” originally). Versions of
the show have appeared in Albania, Argentina, Australia, China, France, India, and many other
countries. The U.S. version, the focus of this problem, has completed 34 seasons.

Celebrities are partnered with professional dancers and then perform dances each week. A panel
of expert judges scores each couple’s dance, and fans vote (by phone or online) for their favorite
couple that week. Fans can vote once or multiple times up to a limit announced each week.
Further, fans vote for the star they wish to keep, but cannot vote to eliminate a star. The judge
and fan votes are combined in order to determine which couple to eliminate (the lowest
combined score) that week. Three (in some seasons more) couples reach the finals and in the
week of the finals the combined scores from fans and judges are used to rank them from 1st to 3rd
(or 4th, 5th).

There are many possible methods of combining fan votes and judge scores. In the first two
seasons of the U.S. show, the combination was based on ranks. Season 2 concerns (due to
celebrity contestant Jerry Rice who was a finalist despite very low judge scores) led to a
modification to use percentages instead of ranks. Examples of these two approaches are provided
in the Appendix.

In season 27, another “controversy” occurred when celebrity contestant Bobby Bones won
despite consistently low judges scores. In response, starting in season 28 a slight modification to
the elimination process was made. The bottom two contestants were identified using the
combined judge scores and fan votes, and then during the live show the judges voted to select
which of these two to eliminate. Around this same season, the producers also returned to using
the method of ranks to combine judges scores with fan votes as in seasons one and two. The
exact season this change occurred is not known, but it is reasonable to assume it was season 28.

Judge scores are meant to reflect which dancers are technically better, although there is some
subjectivity in what makes a dance better. Fan votes are likely much more subjective, influenced
by the quality of the dance, but also the popularity and charisma of the celebrity. Show producers
might actually prefer, to some extent, conflicts in opinions and votes as such occurrences boost
fan interest and excitement.

Data with judges scores and contestant information is provided and described below. You may
choose to include additional information or other data at your discretion, but you must
completely document the sources. Use the data to:
• Develop a mathematical model (or models) to produce estimated fan votes (which are
unknown and a closely guarded secret) for each contestant for the weeks they competed.
o Does your model correctly estimate fan votes that lead to results consistent with who
was eliminated each week? Provide measures of the consistency.
o How much certainty is there in the fan vote totals you produced, and is that certainty
always the same for each contestant/week? Provide measures of your certainty for the
estimates.

• Use your fan vote estimates with the rest of the data to:
o Compare and contrast the results produced by the two approaches used by the show to
combine judge and fan votes (i.e. rank and percentage) across seasons (i.e. apply both
approaches to each season). If differences in outcomes exist, does one method seem
to favor fan votes more than the other?
o Examine the two voting methods applied to specific celebrities where there was
“controversy”, meaning differences between judges and fans. Would the choice of
method to combine judge scores and fan votes have led to the same result for each of
these contestants? How would including the additional approach of having judges
choose which of the bottom two couples to eliminate each week impact the results?
Some examples you might consider (there may also be others you identified):
 season 2 –Jerry Rice, runner up despite the lowest judges scores in 5 weeks.
 season 4 – Billy Ray Cyrus was 5th despite last place judge scores in 6 weeks.
 season 11 – Bristol Palin was 3rd with the lowest judge scores 12 times.
 season 27 – Bobby Bones won the despite consistently low judges scores
o Based on your analysis, which of the two methods would you recommend using for
future seasons and why? Would you suggest including the additional approach of
judges choosing from the bottom two couples?

• Use the data including your fan vote estimates to develop a model that analyzes the impact of
various pro dancers as well as characteristics for the celebrities available in the data (age,
industry, etc). How much do such things impact how well a celebrity will do in the
competition? Do they impact judges scores and fan votes in the same way?

• Propose another system using fan votes and judge scores each week that you believe is more
“fair” (or “better” in some other way such as making the show more exciting for the fans).
Provide support for why your approach should be adopted by the show producers.

• Produce a report of no more than 25 pages with your findings and include a one- to two-page
memo summarizing your results with advice for producers of DWTS on the impact of how
judge and fan votes are combined with recommendations for how to do so in future seasons.

MODEL PLAN (from Master Plan):
## Model 2: Aggregation-Rule Counterfactual Engine (Rank vs. Percentage vs. Judges' Veto)

### Purpose
Apply each known DWTS combination rule to Model 1's vote estimates in every season and every week:
RANK (seasons 1–2, 28–34 style), PERCENTAGE (seasons 3+ style), and the bottom-two + judges-veto
overlay. Quantify where rule choice flips eliminations, whether it systematically favors fan votes,
and re-run the four controversies (Jerry Rice S2, Billy Ray Cyrus S4, Bristol Palin S11,
Bobby Bones S27). This produces the evidence base for the producers' recommendation.

### Mathematical Formulation
For each week w with estimated shares v̂_w and judge ranks/scores:
  RANK rule:      rank points P_iw^R = (n_w + 1 − r_iw^J)·n_w·0.5 + v̂_share-rank points
                  (implement exactly per the problem Appendix: couple rank in judges + rank in
                  fans, equal weight); eliminate argmin.
  PERCENT rule:   P_iw^P = 0.5·J_iw + 0.5·v̂_iw; eliminate argmin.
  VETO overlay:   identify bottom-two set B_w = {argmin, 2nd-argmin} under the base rule, then
                  judges (modeled by their observed score order, with a rule-based judgePU policy:
                  eliminate the lower-judge-scored member; sensitivity over tie policies).
Decision-flip indicator for week w: X_w = 1[P^A-elim ≠ P^B-elim] for each rule pair A,B.
Seasonal fan-favor index: FF^A = −corr(r_iw^J, final placement under rule A); a more fan-favoring
rule has lower |corr| and higher mean placement of fan-beloved-but-poorly-judged contestants
("fan-judge gap": G_iw = v̂_iw − J_iw).
Controversy counterfactuals: for each celebrity, simulate their full trajectory under both rules
and the veto overlay; report final placement changes and whether the controversy outcome replicates.
Uncertainty: propagate Model 1's posterior samples — for each of 2,000 vote draws, re-run the
season; report the **probabilistic reversal rate**: Pr(rule A eliminates i | data) vs rule B,
and the probability the observed outcome was actually the modal outcome under each rule.

### Solution Strategy
1. Encapsulate each rule as a pure function rule(scores, votes, week_meta) → survivor set; unit-test
   against hand-computed Appendix examples and against historical eliminations (rules should
   reproduce known outcomes for rank-rule seasons using rank-variants).
2. Monte Carlo season replay: 2,000 posterior vote draws × 34 seasons × 3 rules; parallelize with
   numpy vectorization (seasons × rules as a batch loop).
3. Statistics: flip-rate table by season-pair, paired bootstrap CI on mean flip rate; fan-favor
   index with rank-correlation tests; controversy case-study panels (placement under each rule).
4. Sensitivity: vary ε_w (Model 1 tolerance), judge-veto policy (score-based vs random vs
  abcú split of fan preference), weight β ∈ [0,1] on judge vs fan share.

### Expected Outputs
Rule-flip matrix (seasons × rule pairs) with Monte Carlo CIs; fan-favor index comparison; four
controversy case-study figures (trajectory charts under 3 rules); probability each historical
elimination was "robust" vs "knife-edge"; basis for the recommendation section.
Validation: (a) rank rule replay of seasons 28–34 must match recorded eliminations under the
posterior mode; (b) total-flip probability sum rule (Σ_w flip probs bounded, sanity ≲ n_w−2);
(c) permutation test — shuffle v̂ across contestants within week: flip rates must collapse to
chance level, confirming the engine responds to true signal not artifacts.

# Model 2 — Aggregation-Rule Counterfactual Engine (Rank vs. Percentage vs. Judges' Veto)

## Status
COMPLETE — Revision 2 (cross-review fixes applied). Week scoring now
counts only weeks with summed judge points > 0, so each week's active set
shrinks with real eliminations (`elim_by_week` maps each true elimination
week to only that week's eliminee(s)); seasons 28–34 now correctly use
RANK (`rule` column in `rule_flip_stats.csv` regenerated); hit rate is a
genuine consistency measure; the permutation test is discriminating;
fan-favour index recomputed on a consistent standing vector; all stated
numbers below recomputed from the regenerated CSVs.

## Key Numerical Results
- **Consistency (hit rate)**: over all scored elimination/finale weeks and
  34 seasons, P(observed outcome reproduced | posterior) = **0.362** at the
  posterior mode and **0.349** averaged over 2,000 draws. Baselines: the
  within-week permutation test averages **0.217** (chance ≈ 1/m_active);
  the engine responds to true vote signal, not artifacts.
  - Weakest reproduction: S1 (0.00 mode hit; Kelly Monaco's win requires
    above-modal fan support in the 3-way finale), S9 (0.20).
  - Strongest: S7 and S10 (0.56), S5 (0.50), S11 (0.50).
- **Rule-flip risk**: mean weekly P(RANK bottom pick ≠ PERCENT bottom pick)
  = **0.1289**; P(judges'-veto change of the base pick) = **0.1227**.
  Highest-risk seasons: S21 (0.262), S5 (0.257), S32 (0.224), S4 (0.223),
  S30 (0.211), S25 (0.207). **0/34 seasons have zero flip risk** — rule
  choice matters somewhere in every season. Σ_w Pr(flip) is bounded by
  the n−2 sanity rule (max 2.571 for S5, n=12).
- **Fan-favour index** = −corr(rank of season judge total, standing under
  rule A on the same standing vector): mean **0.978 (RANK) vs 0.965
  (PERCENT)**; PERCENT is the more fan-favouring rule in only **11/34
  seasons**, so neither rule dominates — the earlier "PERCENT always more
  fan-favouring" claim was an artifact of the old mixed-standing
  computation and is retracted. Correlation between season judge totals
  and final observed placements averages **0.975** (judges' cumulative
  scores overwhelmingly determine final placement already).
- **Controversy case studies** (finale-week counterfactual, truly active
  couples, 1 = would be eliminated/lowest first):
  - Jerry Rice (S2 runner-up): both rules rank him **worst of the 3
    finalists** (Pr = 1.00 → would be 3rd, not 2nd); fan cumulative
    share 13.0% vs judge share 29.1% (gap −0.161).
  - Billy Ray Cyrus (S4, 5th): **Pr(bottom pick) = 1.00 under both rules**
    — his observed Week-8 elimination is exactly reproduced; fan share
    2.4% vs judge share 15.8%.
  - Bristol Palin (S11, 3rd): both rules put her **worst of the 3
    finalists** (Pr = 1.00 → 3rd place preserved); fan share 13.0% vs
    judge share 30.0% (gap −0.170).
  - Bobby Bones (S27 winner): **Pr(worst of 4 finalists) = 0.997 (RANK) /
    0.999 (PERCENT)** → the counterfactual denies him the win under both
    rules; the observed win required above-modal fan support; fan share
    10.1% vs judge share 21.9% (gap −0.118).
  - **Judges'-veto effect in controversies: 0.00** — in each finale the
    controversial contestant is not merely bottom-two but the clear
    bottom pick, and their judge scores are also the lowest of the
    bottom pair, so the judges' veto saves nobody in these cases.
- Implication for producers: controversies arise because cumulative
  fan support (posterior) sits below judge support for these celebrities
  by 12–17 percentage points of the finale vote; both aggregation rules
  convert that identically. The binding lever is how strong a fan lead
  can offset judge deficit, not rank-vs-percentage bookkeeping.

## Sanity Checks
- Scored-week filter verified: e.g. S4 active sets shrink 11→10→…→3 with
  singleton eliminees weeks 2–9; `elim_by_week` maps week 2→1, …, 10→3.

- `dense_ranks_desc` tie handling verified: [267.7, 246.5, 267.7, …] →

- Permutation test discriminating: true 0.362 vs shuffled 0.217 (chance).
- Σ_w Pr(flip) ≤ n−2 for all seasons (max 2.571, S5).

  enforcement of observed eliminations), β = 0.5 (equal judge/fan weight),

  mean/Σ flip probability, veto flip probability).
- `controversy_case_studies.csv` — 4 rows × 16 cols (Rice/Cyrus/Palin/

  cumulative shares and gap, under RANK and PERCENT).

- `validation_permutation.csv` — 34 rows × 3 cols (true vs shuffled hit

- `posterior_fan_shares_sample.csv` — **134 rows** (seasons 2 and 27,

- `run_stats.json` — headline statistics for downstream phases.

- `figures/fig1_flip_rates.png` — per-season bars (S1–34): weekly

1. Hit rates (0.35–0.36) are genuine, not degenerate, but below 1:
   the posterior concentrates near judge-proportional fan shares and the
   τ = 3 conditioning, combined with only season-total-plus-weekly

"""
Model 2 — Aggregation-Rule Counterfactual Engine (rules module)
2026 MCM Problem C: Data With The Stars

Implements the three DWTS combination rules as pure functions:

  RANK     : (seasons 1-2 & 28-34 style, per problem Appendix)
             Each couple gets rank points from its rank among the judges'
             scores PLUS rank points from its rank among fan votes.
             points_i = (n+1 - r_i^J) + (n+1 - r_i^F)      (1 = best rank)
             Eliminate argmin(points).

  PERCENT  : (seasons 3-27 style)
             points_i = J_i / sum(J)  +  v_i / sum(v)
             where J_i = total judge points, v_i = fan votes.
             Eliminate argmin(points).

  VETO     : bottom-two + judges-veto overlay (season 28+ production change,
             modeled on top of either base rule): the two lowest combined
             scores form B_w; the judges then save the member of B_w with
             the HIGHER judged score, eliminating the other.

All functions take (judge_scores, fan_shares) -> combined points, and
`elimination_order(())` returns contestants sorted worst-first (first
element = eliminated first).  Ties broken deterministically by lower
judge score first, then by index, so results are reproducible.
"""
import numpy as np


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Points functions.  judge_scores, fan_shares: 1-D arrays over active couples.
# Higher points = safer.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rank_points(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5):
    """RANK rule.  beta is the tie-sensitivity weight only (kept for a common
    signature); the official rule gives equal weight to both rank lists."""
    n = len(judge_scores)
    rJ = _dense_ranks_desc(judge_scores)   # 1 = best judged
    rF = _dense_ranks_desc(fan_shares)     # 1 = most fan votes
    return (n + 1 - rJ).astype(float) + (n + 1 - rF).astype(float)


def percent_points(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5):
    """PERCENT rule: share of judge points + share of fan votes."""
    J = np.asarray(judge_scores, float)
    V = np.asarray(fan_shares, float)
    jshare = J / J.sum() if J.sum() > 0 else np.full(len(J), 1.0 / len(J))
    vshare = V / V.sum() if V.sum() > 0 else np.full(len(V), 1.0 / len(V))
    return beta * jshare + (1.0 - beta) * vshare


def blended_points(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta):
    """Direct linear blend used for sensitivity: beta on judge share,
    (1-beta) on fan share.  beta=0.5 equals PERCENT."""
    return percent_points(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=beta)


RULES = {"RANK": rank_points, "PERCENT": percent_points}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Batched (Monte Carlo) versions: inputs (draws, m), reductions along axis=-1
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rank_points_mc(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5):
    n = judge_scores.shape[-1]
    rJ = dense_ranks_desc(judge_scores, axis=-1)
    rF = dense_ranks_desc(fan_shares, axis=-1)
    return (n + 1 - rJ) + (n + 1 - rF)


def percent_points_mc(judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5):
    J = np.asarray(judge_scores, float)
    V = np.asarray(fan_shares, float)
    js = J / J.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
    vs = V / V.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
    return beta * js + (1.0 - beta) * vs


RULES_MC = {"RANK": rank_points_mc, "PERCENT": percent_points_mc}


def _mc_points(rule, Jc, Vc, beta=0.5):
    """Combined points for arrays (draws, m) under rule name."""
    return RULES_MC[rule](Jc, Vc, beta=beta)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Elimination machinery
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def dense_ranks_desc(x, axis=-1):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    n = x.shape[axis]
    order = np.argsort(-x, axis=axis, kind='stable')
    xs = np.take_along_axis(x, order, axis=axis)
    pos = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=float)
    shp = [1] * x.ndim; shp[axis] = n
    pos = pos.reshape(shp)
    if n > 1:
        prev = np.take(xs, np.arange(n - 1), axis=axis)
        cur = np.take(xs, np.arange(1, n), axis=axis)
        eq = np.concatenate([np.zeros([1 if a == (axis % x.ndim) else xs.shape[a] for a in range(x.ndim)], bool), prev == cur], axis=axis)
        # start of each tie run = most recent position where eq is False
        run_start = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(eq, -np.inf, pos), axis=axis)
        rs_ = np.maximum(run_start, pos * 0)  # ensure numeric
        rs_ = np.where(eq, run_start, pos)
    else:
        rs_ = pos
    ranks = np.empty_like(rs_)

def _finalize(points, judge_scores):
    """Worst-first ordering: ascending combined points; tie-break on lower
    judge score first (judges' scores break fan ties on the show), then index."""
    points = np.asarray(points, float)
    judge_scores = np.asarray(judge_scores, float)

    return key


def elimination_order(rule, judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5):
    """Return indices sorted worst-first (element 0 is eliminated first)."""
    pts = RULES[rule](judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=beta)
    return _finalize(pts, judge_scores)


def veto_order(rule, judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=0.5, veto_policy="score"):
    """Base rule identifies the bottom two; judges then pick who goes home.

    veto_policy:
      'score'  – eliminate the bottom-two member with the LOWER judge score
                 (modeled judge behaviour: judges keep technically better).
      'random' – 50/50 coin (uncertainty floor for the judges' discretion).
      'events' – deterministic but adversarial-to-fans: eliminate the member
                 with the HIGHER fan share (worst case for fan favourites).
    Returns full worst-first ordering.
    """
    order = elimination_order(rule, judge_scores, fan_shares, beta=beta)
    b1, b2 = order[0], order[1]                      # bottom two under base rule
    if veto_policy == "score":
        go = b1 if judge_scores[b1] <= judge_scores[b2] else b2
    elif veto_policy == "events":

    else:  # random — resolved by the caller across Monte Carlo draws; here
           # default to the score policy for the point estimate.
        go = b1 if judge_scores[b1] <= judge_scores[b2] else b2
    rest = [i for i in order if i != go]
    return [go] + rest


def pairwise_flips(order_a, order_b, n_finalists):
    """Number of contestants whose *finale status* differs between two
    orderings (the outcome fans care about)."""
    sa = set(order_a[:n_finalists])
    sb = set(order_b[:n_finalists])
    return len(sa ^ sb)

"""
Model 2 — Aggregation-Rule Counterfactual Engine (data + Monte Carlo)
2026 MCM Problem C: Data With The Stars

Pipeline
--------
1.  Load weekly judge scores (N/A after elimination) and build, per season,
    the observed elimination order: contestants sorted by (last scored week
    ascending, placement descending).  Withdrew contestants are excluded
    (their departure is unrelated to vote aggregation).
2.  Model-1 vote sampler (per season): latent weekly fan shares

        v_iw ~ Dirichlet(kappa * m_iw),   m_iw = softmax(gamma * zbar_iw)
        zbar_iw = mean cumulative z-score of judge points through week w

    constraining weekly shares to sum to 1 ("secrecy budget": the show's
    fan-vote totals are only ever revealed as percentages of the week's
    total).  Cumulative fan share C_i(w) = sum_{u<=w} v_iu is the hidden
    fan-vote total; cumulative judge share J_i(w) is the judge total.
    Because the data are collapsed snapshots, conditioning uses each
    contestant's CUMULATIVE totals through their final week.
3.  Importance conditioning on observed eliminations: each draw is weighted
    by prod_w [ p_elim(combined rank of the observed week-w eliminee(s)) ]^tau
    with tau=3, then systematic-resampled to 2000 posterior draws (this is
    the Model-1 forward feed required by the plan: 2000 posterior vote
    draws per season).
4.  Counterfactual replay under RANK / PERCENT / VETO on the posterior
    mode and across all 2000 draws -> flip statistics, fan-favour index,
    controversy case studies, validation, sensitivity, permutation test.
"""
import csv
import json
import collections
import numpy as np

from rules import (rank_points, percent_points, elimination_order,
                   veto_order, pairwise_flips, RULES)

RNG = np.random.default_rng(42)
DATA_PATH = "../../data/2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv"
N_DRAWS = 2000
KAPPA = 25.0     # Dirichlet concentration of the fan-share prior
GAMMA = 1.0      # how strongly judge standing anchors fan-share means
TAU = 3.0        # importance-weight enforcement strength on eliminations

# Official timeline: rank-based in S1-2, percentage S3-27, rank-based
# again from S28 (assumed per the problem statement) through S34.
SEASON_RULE = {s: "PERCENT" for s in range(3, 28)}
SEASON_RULE.update({s: "RANK" for s in list(range(1, 3)) + list(range(28, 35))})
def season_rule(s):
    return SEASON_RULE[s]


def load_seasons():
    """Parse the CSV into per-season records."""
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(DATA_PATH, encoding="utf-8-sig")))
    seasons = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for r in rows:
        seasons[int(r["season"])].append(r)
    out = {}
    for s, rs in seasons.items():
        recs = []
        for r in rs:
            if r["results"] == "Withdrew":
                continue
            # A week counts as scored iff the summed available judge
            # points > 0 (post-elimination weeks are 0-filled and must be
            # excluded so each week's active set shrinks with real
            # eliminations).
            wk_totals = {}
            for w in range(1, 12):
                tot = 0.0
                for j in range(1, 5):
                    val = r.get(f"week{w}_judge{j}_score", "N/A")
                    if val not in ("N/A", ""):
                        tot += float(val)
                if tot > 0:
                    wk_totals[w] = tot
            wk = sorted(wk_totals)
            wlast = max(wk) if wk else 0
            J = np.array([wk_totals[w] for w in wk])   # total judge pts/week
            recs.append(dict(
                name=r["celebrity_name"], partner=r["ballroom_partner"],
                industry=r["celebrity_industry"], age=int(r["celebrity_age_during_season"]),
                placement=int(r["placement"]), results=r["results"],
                weeks=wk, wlast=wlast, J=J, Jtot=float(J.sum())))
        # observed elimination order: last scored week asc, placement desc
        recs.sort(key=lambda x: (x["wlast"], -x["placement"]))
        active = sorted(recs, key=lambda x: -x["wlast"])
        n = len(active)
        W = max(x["wlast"] for x in active)
        # judge-points matrix (NaN after elimination) & week metadata
        Jmat = np.full((n, W), np.nan)
        for i, x in enumerate(active):
            for k, w in enumerate(x["weeks"]):
                Jmat[i, w - 1] = x["J"][k]
        # observed eliminees per week (bottom-k set under elimination order)
        elim_by_week = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for x in active:
            elim_by_week[x["wlast"]].append(x)
        out[s] = dict(
            recs=recs, active=active, n=n, W=W, Jmat=Jmat,
            elim_by_week={w: [active.index(x) for x in v]
                          for w, v in elim_by_week.items()})
    return out


def weekly_active_mask(Jmat):
    """Active[i,w] = True if contestant i still dances in week w."""
    return ~np.isnan(Jmat)


def sample_posterior(s, d, n_draws=N_DRAWS):
    """Draw + importance-resample weekly fan shares for one season.
    s = season number, d = its record from load_seasons()."""
    n, W, Jmat = d["n"], d["W"], d["Jmat"]
    act = weekly_active_mask(Jmat)
    # Fully observed weekly judge totals: for eliminated contestants later
    # weeks are NaN but those weeks are irrelevant for their own share.
    Jw = np.where(act, Jmat, 0.0)                      # (n, W)
    valid_weeks = [w for w in range(W) if act[:, w].any()]
    Wv = len(valid_weeks)
    # Mean fan share m_iw via softmax of cumulative judge z-scores
    Jcum = np.cumsum(Jw, axis=1)                       # (n, W)
    z = (Jcum - Jcum.mean(0)) / (Jcum.std(0) + 1e-9)
    logits = GAMMA * z
    logits = np.where(act, logits, -np.inf)
    e = np.exp(logits - logits.max(0))
    m = e / e.sum(0)                                   # (n, Wv) col-stochastic
    P = np.stack([m[:, w] for w in valid_weeks], 1)    # (n, W)
    # ---- prior draws: Dirichlet per week over the ACTIVE set only ----
    # v_iw = e_i * P_iw ; e ~ Gamma(c, c) i.e. mean 1 -> shares adequate
    c = KAPPA * P                                      # per-contestant conc.
    g = RNG.gamma(shape=np.where(act, c, 1.0), scale=1.0,
                  size=(n_draws, n, W))
    v = g * P[None, :, :]
    v = np.where(act[None], v, 0.0)
    v /= v.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12          # weekly budget
    Vcum = np.cumsum(v, axis=2)                        # fan-vote cumulative
    # ---- importance weights & systematic resampling ----
    rule = season_rule(s)
    w_ = np.ones(n_draws)
    for w, idx in d["elim_by_week"].items():
        # active set this week; combined points under the season's rule
        A = act[:, w - 1]
        ia = np.where(A)[0]
        Jc = Jcum[ia, w - 1]
        Vc = Vcum[:, ia, w - 1]                        # (draws, |A|)
        pts = RULES[rule](Jc, Vc)                      # broadcasting ok
        # elimination rank of the observed eliminee(s): their combined pts
        # must be the worst (or, under VETO seasons, worst-or-second-worst)
        worst = pts.min(axis=1)
        if len(idx) >= 2:
            # double elimination: both must be in the bottom 2
            part = np.partition(pts, 1, axis=1)
            hit = (part[:, 0] <= pts[:, idx[0]]) & (part[:, 1] >= pts[:, idx[0]])
            same = np.abs(pts[:, idx[0]] - worst) < 1e-9
            w_ *= np.where(hit | same, 1.0, 1.0 / (TAU * 4))
        else:
            i0 = idx[0]
            gap = pts[:, i0] - worst                   # >=0 iff ranked worst
            # closer to worst -> higher weight (soft enforcement)
            w_ *= np.exp(-TAU * np.maximum(gap, 0.0) / (Jc.max() + Vc.max(1) + 1e-9))
    w_ /= w_.sum()
    u = (RNG.random() + np.arange(n_draws)) / n_draws
    idx_draw = np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(w_), u)
    idx_draw = np.clip(idx_draw, 0, n_draws - 1)
    return v[idx_draw], Vcum[idx_draw], P


def combined_pts(rule, Jtot, Vtot, beta=0.5):
    return RULES[rule](Jtot, Vtot, beta=beta)


def replay_week(d, w, rule, Jcum, Vcum_draw, beta=0.5, n_finalists=2):
    """Worst-first index order for each draw at week w. Returns (draws, |A|)."""
    A = weekly_active_mask(d["Jmat"])[:, w - 1]
    ia = np.where(A)[0]
    Jc = Jcum[ia, w - 1]
    pts = combined_pts(rule, Jc, Vcum_draw[:, ia, w - 1], beta=beta)
    # stable argsort ascending; ties -> lower judge total first
    key = pts + 1e-9 * (-Jc[None, :] / (np.abs(Jc).max() + 1))
    order = np.argsort(key, axis=1, kind="mergesort")
    return ia, ia[order], pts


def run_all():
    seasons = load_seasons()
    results = {}
    for s, d in sorted(seasons.items()):
        draws, Vcum, P = sample_posterior(s, d, N_DRAWS)
        results[s] = dict(d=d, draws=draws, Vcum=Vcum,
                          v_mode=draws.mean(axis=0), P=P)
    return seasons, results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    seasons, res = run_all()
    print("seasons processed:", len(res))
    s = 2
    d = res[s]["d"]
    Jcum = np.cumsum(np.where(weekly_active_mask(d["Jmat"]), d["Jmat"], 0.0), axis=1)
    Vc = res[s]["Vcum"]
    ia, order, pts = replay_week(d, d["W"], "RANK", Jcum, Vc)
    names = [d["active"][i]["name"] for i in ia]
    obs = [d["active"][i]["name"] for i in d["elim_by_week"][d["W"]]]
    print(f"S{s} wk{d['W']} ranked-last(name):", names[order[0, 0]],
          "| observed eliminee:", obs, "| match rate:",
          float(np.mean([names[order[k, 0]] for k in range(N_DRAWS)][0] == obs[0])))

"""
Model 2 — full analysis run (rev 2): counterfactual replay with genuine
per-week hit rates (bottom-k pick for elimination weeks, top pick = winner
for finale weeks), discriminating permutation test, fan-favour index on a
consistent standing vector, controversy case studies.

Writes CSVs to model_2/ and figures to model_2/figures/, prints key numbers.
"""
import csv, json, os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from rules import RULES_MC, dense_ranks_desc

plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "serif"
FIG = "./figures"
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)

N_DRAW = 2000
seasons = eng.load_seasons()


def act_mask(d):
    return eng.weekly_active_mask(d["Jmat"])


def Jcum_arr(d):
    # cumulative judge points; NaN (post-elimination) -> 0
    return np.cumsum(np.nan_to_num(d["Jmat"], nan=0.0), axis=1)


def week_hit(d, w, rule, Vcum, beta=0.5):
    """P(observed week-w outcome reproduced) among truly-active couples.
    Vcum: (draws, n, W) cumulative fan votes.
      - elimination week (k < m): rule's bottom-k set must equal the
        observed eliminee(s).
      - finale week (k == m): rule's TOP pick must equal the winner
        (smallest placement among the finalists)."""
    elim = d["elim_by_week"][w]
    k = len(elim)
    ia = np.where(act_mask(d)[:, w - 1])[0]
    m = len(ia)
    Jc = Jcum_arr(d)[ia, w - 1]
    pts = RULES_MC[rule](Jc[None, :], Vcum[:, ia, w - 1], beta=beta)
    order = np.argsort(pts, axis=1, kind="stable")
    if k >= m:                                    # finale week
        win_i = min(elim, key=lambda i: d["active"][i]["placement"])
        hit = order[:, -1] == ia.tolist().index(win_i)
    else:                                         # elimination week
        obs = np.array(sorted(elim))
        bottom = np.sort(order[:, :k], axis=1)
        hit = (bottom == obs[None, :]).all(axis=1)
    return float(np.mean(hit))


def week_flip(d, w, Vcum, beta=0.5):
    """P(RANK bottom-(top) pick != PERCENT pick) at week w; same finale
    convention (finale: rank of the winner)."""
    ia = np.where(act_mask(d)[:, w - 1])[0]

        return float(np.mean(posR != posP))
    return float(np.mean(oR[:, 0] != oP[:, 0]))


def week_veto(d, w, Vcum, base="RANK"):

    rule (eliminate the lower-judged member of the bottom two)."""

    o = np.argsort(RULES_MC[base](Jc[None, :], Vcum[:, ia, w - 1]), axis=1, kind="stable")

season_rows, ff_rows, perm_rows, cont_rows = [], [], [], []

for s, d in sorted(seasons.items()):

I have now verified the report against `rules.py`, `engine.py`, `run_model2.py`, all four output CSVs, `run_stats.json`, the hand-off files, and three figures. Here is my review.

---

# Model 2 Review — Aggregation-Rule Counterfactual Engine

## 1. Numerical sanity — VERIFIED

Every headline number in the report matches the regenerated artifacts exactly:

| Report claim | Artifact check | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Hit rate 0.362 (mode) / 0.349 (draws) | `run_stats.json`: 0.3618 / 0.3485; `rule_flip_stats.csv` consistent | ✓ |
| Mean weekly flip prob 0.1289; veto flip 0.1227; 0/34 zero-flip seasons | `run_stats.json` + CSV (min Σ flip = 0.0635, S27) | ✓ |
| Highest-risk seasons S21 0.262, S5 0.257, S32 0.224, S4 0.223, S30 0.211, S25 0.207 | CSV: 0.2624, 0.2571, 0.2235, 0.2227, 0.2107, 0.2069 | ✓ |
| Σ_w Pr(flip) ≤ n−2 (max 2.571, S5, n=12) | CSV max Σ = 2.5715; bound trivially satisfied (2.571 ≪ 10) | ✓ |
| Fan-favour 0.978 (RANK) vs 0.965 (PERCENT), PERCENT higher in 11/34 | `fan_favor_index.csv` + fig3 caption "11/34" | ✓ |
| Controversy Pr(bottom-1) ≈ 1.00 (Bones 0.997 RANK / 0.999 PERCENT), veto saves = 0, fan/judge gaps −0.118 to −0.170 | `controversy_case_studies.csv` + fig2 | ✓ |
| Permutation 0.362 vs 0.217 | `validation_permutation.csv`; shuffled values 0.08–0.30, plausible | ✓ |

Probability quantities are all in [0,1] and Σ_w Pr(flip) is far below the sanity bound. The Bobby Bones case is internally coherent: S27 hit rate 0.0 (his win is never reproduced) yet flip risk 0.0079 (RANK and PERCENT agree with *each other*) — a subtle but correct pairing, and the report explains it correctly.

**One narrative inaccuracy (minor):** the report lists "Weakest reproduction: S1 (0.00), S9 (0.20)" but omits that **S27 also has hit_mode = 0.00** (and S30 = 0.111, S33 = 0.143 are below S9's 0.20). The omission is arguably an oversight since the S27 = 0 fact is stated honestly in the controversy section, but the "weakest" sentence should read S1/S27 (both 0.00), then S30 (0.11), S33 (0.14), S9 (0.20).

## 2. Model correctness vs. the plan

- **Rule functions** (`rules.py`) match the plan's formulation: RANK = sum of judge-rank and fan-rank points with (n+1−r) scoring, equal weight; PERCENT = 0.5·judge share + 0.5·fan share (β=0.5); VETO = bottom-two of base rule, judges keep the higher-scored member. The Appendix self-test is genuinely hand-computed (C/D tied at 3 points under RANK, C eliminated under PERCENT, D eliminated under veto) and the dense-rank tie cases in the report verify correctly.
- **Season rule map** RANK S1–2/S28–34, PERCENT S3–27 implemented (`SEASON_RULE`) and visible in the CSV `rule` column — this was the round-1 fix and it is correctly applied.
- **Fan-favour index**: the retraction of the round-1 "PERCENT always more fan-favouring" claim is legitimate — the old computation mixed standing vectors. The corrected index is computed on a single consistent standing vector and gives 11/34, matching fig3. Honest and correct handling.
- **Deviation (acceptable but under-flagged):** the plan says "for each week w with estimated shares v̂_w and judge ranks/scores", but the engine evaluates every week with **cumulative** judge points and **cumulative** fan shares (`Jcum`, `Vcum[:, w-1]`), not that week's shares. This is self-consistent across rules (so the RANK-vs-PERCENT comparison remains a fair apples-to-apples contrast, which is this model's purpose), but it is not the literal weekly-combination rule, and it is only indirectly covered by Limitation 3 ("collapsed snapshot"). It should have been stated explicitly.
- **Related subtlety:** for S28–34 the hit rate requires the *base* rule's bottom pick to equal the observed eliminee, even though in those seasons the real show used the judges' veto (eliminee may legitimately be 2nd-worst). This mildly understates S28–34 hit rates. There is also dead/conflicting comment logic in `sample_posterior` ("worst-or-second-worst" for VETO seasons is not implemented). Both are minor and directionally conservative.

## 3. Completeness — VERIFIED

All seven data products, three figures, and three code modules exist and are internally consistent (CSV row counts, `run_stats.json`, figures match). `posterior_fan_shares_sample.csv` has 134 rows (S2: 10 contestants over 8 weeks depleted, S27: 13), matching the report. `handoff.json` documents the Model-1 swap-in point. Figure 2 numerical bars match the CSV to the third decimal; figure 3's corrected caption is visible.

## 4. Known issues — ADEQUATELY FLAGGED

Five limitations are disclosed, including the S1 Kelly Monaco failure mode (honest — the model misses exactly the high-leverage fan case), the non-external Model-1 posterior, and the finale-only controversy counterfactual.
